authority.statement: ARCH-1 classifies ESI-1 symbols deterministically for architecture cleanup/ownership visibility. It never authorizes deletion by itself and cannot weaken build, test, Kodex or runtime gates.

A.label: Loeschbar
A.meaning: Within the complete ESI-1 source scope, a private free function has no lexical reference, no incoming unique-name call edge, no productive reachability, and no cfg/export/test/bench/proc-macro/used-sensitive attribute in its declaration context.
A.fail_closed: Any unresolved prerequisite yields OFFEN, not A.

B.label: Zusammenfuehrbar / redundant
B.meaning: An explicitly legacy/obsolete/deprecated/shadow-named symbol that is itself still bound by reachability/reference evidence has a deterministic same-file counterpart target that is productively reachable or referenced.
B.fail_closed: No concrete target yields no B classification.

C.label: Notwendige Unterstuetzung
C.meaning: A symbol is productively reachable without an ARCH-1 D authority rule, or is explicitly bound test/tool support under the fixed rules.

D.label: Autoritativer Kern
D.meaning: A productively reachable entrypoint or explicitly named Writer-Authority/Owner, Selection-Authority/Owner, Canonical-Authority/Owner or Governance gate path matches a versioned ARCH-1 rule.

OFFEN.label: Nicht sicher entscheidbar
OFFEN.meaning: No A/B/C/D rule has sufficient static evidence. OFFEN is the mandatory fail-closed default.

removed_legacy_class: N is not part of ARCH-1. Legacy AIC-1 A/B/C/N/OFFEN classifications are not comparable to ARCH-1.

comparability.rule: A/B/C/D/OFFEN counts are directly comparable only when architecture_contract_version is identical. ARCH-1 -> ARCH-2 is an explicit classification-series break.

deletion_boundary: Class A is a static architecture statement inside ESI-1 scope, not a command to mutate source. Actual removal still requires normal EtuSchlopf change control and gates.
